findings.title: Members endpoint now caps all groups at 50, but the public group members page has no pagination
findings.body: Before this change, GroupsController#members returned every member for non-automatic groups and only applied limit/offset to automatic groups (default 200). Now every group is limited to 50 by default. The public group members page (discourse/routes/group-members.js.es6 calling model.findMembers() once, rendering templates/group/members.hbs) has no next/previous or load-more controls — only the admin template got pagination. As a result, any group with more than 50 members (and any automatic group with more than 50, previously 200) now only ever shows the first 50 alphabetically, and the remaining members are unreachable. Either keep returning the full roster for the public page or add pagination there.

findings.title: PATCH /admin/groups/:id now silently ignores incremental membership changes and resets visible to false
findings.body: The old update dispatched PATCH requests to update_patch, which applied params[:changes] (add/delete usernames) and touched nothing else. This PR removes that branch, so PATCH and PUT both run the single update action: params[:changes] is silently ignored while success_json is returned, and because visible is computed unconditionally as params[:visible] == "true", any legacy client sending an incremental membership PATCH without a visible param will silently flip the group to invisible. If the incremental API is being removed, the action should reject such requests rather than report success, and visible should not be forced to false when the parameter is absent.

findings.title: totalPages is off by one when user_count is an exact multiple of limit
findings.body: totalPages is computed as Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1, which yields an extra page when user_count divides evenly (e.g. 100 users with limit 50 gives 3 pages instead of 2). On the real last page "next" stays enabled (showingLast compares currentPage to the inflated totalPages); clicking it requests offset == user_count, the server returns an empty member list, and the admin sees an empty "3/3" page. Use Math.ceil(user_count / limit).

findings.title: automatic does not resolve inside the member item view, so the remove link is rendered for automatic groups too
findings.body: This template is rendered as the itemView of {{each member in members itemView="group-member"}}, so its scope is the member item view (which only has `member` set via the each keyword), not the adminGroup controller. `automatic` is a property of the group, so {{#unless automatic}} is always truthy and the × remove link renders even for automatic groups. Clicking it sends DELETE /admin/groups/:id/members; the server correctly returns 422, but Group#removeMember has no rejection handler, so the admin gets no feedback and the row simply stays. The group's automatic flag needs to be passed into the item view explicitly, and/or the failure should be surfaced.

findings.title: remove_member automatic-group spec uses PUT although the route only accepts DELETE
findings.body: The "cannot remove members from automatic groups" example issues `xhr :put, :remove_member, group_id: 1, user_id: 42`, but config/routes.rb maps remove_member only for DELETE ("delete 'members'"); PUT members routes to add_members. Controller specs dispatch straight to the action, so the test passes anyway, but it no longer reflects real traffic and would not fail if the route/verb mapping were broken. Use `xhr :delete` here, matching the other remove_member example.
